usageNotes: Use this to obtain a SPICE connection ticket for a running LXC container; the returned object (host, tls-port, password, proxy, type) can be passed directly to 'remote-viewer' or a compatible SPICE client. The container must be running and the target node must be online; the caller requires the VM.Console privilege on /vms/{vmid}. The optional 'proxy' parameter should be set to the hostname or IP the client will use to reach the SPICE proxy — omit it to default to the node where the container is currently running.

examples.summary: Get SPICE config for LXC 200 on node pve1, with proxy hint matching the API host

tips: Pass the full response object directly to 'remote-viewer' via a .vv file or stdin — no manual field mapping needed.

If the SPICE window never opens, confirm the container has a console device configured (e.g. lxc.console.size set or Proxmox default tty); pure network-only containers may not expose a usable console.
The password in the response is a short-lived one-time token; request a fresh proxy config each time a session is opened rather than caching it.
All cluster nodes run spiceproxy on port 3128 by default — set 'proxy' to whichever node is reachable from the client's network segment.
